title: Driver
description: What a driver offers, as data: the element type it serves, what a clip may ask of it and how the element is set up. One file per element type in drivers/. Its implementation lives in the runtimes.

elementType.description: The type of the elements it serves, as .hw files write it (pwm_output); the file is named after it.

conflictPolicy.description: What happens when two sequences on one priority command the element: the latest command wins (lights, relays), or one sequence owns it while it runs (motors, servos). Needed by a driver with actions.

safeState.description: The action the element rests in: when nothing commands it, on stop, on panic. One of its actions that needs no arguments. Needed by a driver with actions.

config.description: The options an element of this type takes in a .hw file, beyond its wiring.

actions.description: What a clip may ask of the element. None for an element that only reads.

driverAction.description: An action of the element, with the parameters a clip gives it and the state it leaves the element in.

endState.description: The state the action leaves the element in: what an instant command sets, and where a clip with a length ends.

startState.description: The state a clip with a length starts from, for an action that moves the element from one state to another over its clip (a fade). Without it the action holds its end state for the whole clip.

driverParameter.description: A parameter of an action or an option of an element's configuration: its type, its limits and the value it takes when not given. Without a default it must be given, unless it is optional.

min.description: The lowest value allowed on every board (numbers only, with max). What only a board limits is in its profile.

max.description: The highest value allowed (numbers only, with min).

optional.description: May be left out with nothing in its place: the driver then decides (a fade without a from starts where the element is). Never with a default.

actionState.description: A state of the element as a level, from 0 (off) to 100 (fully on): the level itself, or the name of the parameter of the action that gives it.
